# Image + Article

`editorial/image-article` &middot; section-level &middot; category: editorial

## Purpose

An image with the article text: heading, byline, body copy and an optional button. Image on top or beside the text.

## Required fields

| Field | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `image` | image { src, alt } |  |
| `heading` | text |  |
| `body` | richtext |  |

## Optional fields

| Field | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `byline` | text |  |
| `cta` | cta { label, href } |  |

## Variants

Same data and structure, different styling. Pick one with `{ variant: 'name' }`.

- **default**: Image on top.
- **image-left**: Image on the left of the text. Sets `layout: left`.
- **image-right**: Image on the right of the text. Sets `layout: right`.

## Settings

Every setting has a default. Values may be token references (`@colors.accent`, `@theme.card.radius`). Pass overrides with `{ settings: { ... } }`.

| Setting | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hideOnMobile` | boolean | `false` |
| `hideOnDesktop` | boolean | `false` |
| `layout` | one of `top`, `left`, `right` | `"top"` |
| `background` | color | `"@colors.surface"` |
| `padding` | spacing | `"@theme.section.paddingY @theme.section.paddingX @theme.section.paddingY @theme.section.paddingX"` |

## Responsive behavior

- `hideOnMobile`: hides it below 480px. Outlook desktop and Gmail on non-Google accounts ignore media queries and still show it.
- `hideOnDesktop`: shows it only on phones. Clients that ignore media queries keep it hidden.

## Compatibility

| Outlook desktop | Gmail apps | Dark mode |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text and images honored. Side variants are a table row. | Fine. Side variants stack on phones through a media query. | Swaps via dm-* classes when on the brand surface or background color. |



## Example usage

This is a section-level component: use it directly in an email body or a recipe.

In an email (`.mjml`):

```
[[ c('editorial/image-article', {
  "image": {
    "src": "https://placehold.co/600x320/png?text=Harvest",
    "alt": "Flax fields in bloom under a pale morning sky"
  },
  "heading": "From flax field to finished shirt",
  "byline": "By Maya Chen, 14 June",
  "body": "<p>Every linen shirt starts as a blue-flowered field in Normandy. After harvest the stalks are left to ret in the dew, then scutched, combed and spun.</p><p>The whole process takes about eight months, and almost none of it is automated.</p>",
  "cta": {
    "label": "Read the full story",
    "href": "https://example.com/journal/flax-to-shirt"
  }
}) ]]
```
